BIG PICTURE
Mosaic MAKING TECHNIQUES helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

In this part you learn to create a simple pictorial using • Guided in appreciating own and paper cuts for enjoyment. others work as learners express their. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a simple pictorial using • Guided in appreciating own and paper cuts for enjoyment. others work as learners express their.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Mosaic MAKING TECHNIQUES is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Mosaic MAKING TECHNIQUES to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: create a simple pictorial using • Guided in appreciating own and paper cuts for enjoyment. others work as learners express their.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the sue of locally emotions. available materials in creating pictorials 84.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Mosaic MAKING TECHNIQUES from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Mosaic MAKING TECHNIQUES: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Mosaic MAKING TECHNIQUES?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What should we use to make MAKING leaner should be able to: making mosaic items mosaic items?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Mosaic MAKING TECHNIQUES means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: create a simple pictorial using • Guided in appreciating own and paper cuts for enjoyment. others work as learners express their.
5. Be able to: appreciate the sue of locally emotions. available materials in creating pictorials 84.
